# Monte Carlo validation against NASA CARA

<!-- Generated by tools/validation_report.py; do not edit. -->

**All 33 comparisons pass**: on every case CARA's Monte Carlo Pc lies inside keepout's confidence interval.

keepout's Monte Carlo Pc is compared with CARA's on the cases of [CARA Analysis Tools](https://github.com/nasa/CARA_Analysis_Tools) (commit `1c78beb1f7ae`) that have a Monte Carlo reference: Alfano's test cases and those of CARA's Pc method test set with a large enough Pc.

Both values are estimates from random samples, so they never agree exactly. A case passes when CARA's value lies inside keepout's confidence interval. Each interval is at 99.97% confidence (1 - 0.01 / 33): a correct keepout fails any of the 33 cases with a chance of at most 1%. keepout sizes each case for about 400 expected collisions, so its own sampling error is about 5%; a difference of 5 to 10% from CARA is sampling noise, not disagreement.

## Summary

| Suite | Method | Cases passed | Worst relative error |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alfano (2009), Monte Carlo | montecarlo | 12 / 12 | 2.5e-02 |
| CARA Pc method test set, Monte Carlo | montecarlo | 21 / 21 | 9.5e-02 |

## Not compared

- **53-CDM cases with a CARA Monte Carlo Pc below 1e-04.** keepout
  sizes a Monte Carlo case for about 400 expected collisions.
  Below a Pc of 1e-04 that takes more than 4,000,000 trials,
  the most a case is given, so these cases are left out. The
  [3-D validation](validation.md#cara-pc-method-test-set-3-d) compares Hall's
  3D-Nc with CARA on every case instead.
